source: 37% of films fail - ... 1,494 fail and 2,506 pass
claim: Of the 4,000 films, 1,494 fail the Bechdel test and 2,506 pass, a 37% failure rate.
code: m.rating.agg(films=lambda s: s.size, fail=lambda s: (s < 3).sum(), pass_=lambda s: (s >= 3).sum(), fail_pct=lambda s: round((s < 3).mean() * 100))

source: 53% Fails Test 47% Passes Test ... 38% Fails Test 62% Passes Test ... 0% Fails 100% Passes
claim: Among the highest-grossing films, all-male writing teams fail 53% and pass 47%; teams with at least one woman fail 38% and pass 62%; all-women writing teams fail 0% and pass 100%.
code:
(p[p.role.eq('w') & p.movie_id.isin(m.nlargest(200, 'box_office').movie_id)]
 .assign(gender=lambda d: d.gender.fillna('u'))
 .pivot_table(index='movie_id', columns='gender', values='person_name', aggfunc='count', fill_value=0)
 .rename_axis(columns=None)
 .pipe(lambda d: d.assign(f=d.get('f', 0), m=d.get('m', 0), u=d.get('u', 0)))
 .join(m.set_index('movie_id').rating)
 .pipe(lambda d: pd.concat([
   d[(d.f == 0) & (d.u == 0)].assign(cat='all men'),
   d[d.f >= 1].assign(cat='at least one woman'),
   d[(d.f > 0) & (d.m == 0) & (d.u == 0)].assign(cat='all women')
 ]))
 .groupby('cat').rating.agg(fail_pct=lambda s: (s < 3).mean() * 100, pass_pct=lambda s: (s >= 3).mean() * 100)
 .round(0).astype(int)
)

code:
(p[p.role.eq('w') & p.gender.notna()]
 .merge(m[['movie_id', 'box_office']], on='movie_id')
 .assign(bin=lambda d: pd.cut(d.box_office, [-np.inf, 10e6, 50e6, 100e6, 500e6, np.inf], labels=['$0-$10M', '$11-$50M', '$51-$100M', '$101-$500M', '$500M+']))
 .groupby(['bin', 'gender'], observed=True).size().unstack()
 .assign(ratio=lambda d: (d['m'] / d['f']).round())
)
